annotations.annotation_text: Fraternal archetype "Shaun" on page 442 ("Jaun's Sermon"): the opposing sons — Shem the Penman (introvert artist, tree, darkness) and Shaun the Post (extrovert politician, stone, light) — manifest here within Jaun (Shaun) preaching to the twenty-nine girls, the Ondt and the Gracehoper fable, departure and farewell. Their Brunonian dialectic of coinciding opposites propels the chapter's conflict during this Age of Men phase.
sources: Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe
Norris, Margot. The Decentered Universe of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/decentereduniver0000norr
Gordon, John. Finnegans Wake: A Plot Summary. https://johngordonfinnegan.weebly.com

annotations.annotation_text: Oneiric dimension "night" on page 442 ("Jaun's Sermon"): the nocturnal consciousness surfaces within Jaun (Shaun) preaching to the twenty-nine girls, the Ondt and the Gracehoper fable, departure and farewell. During this Age of Men phase, Joyce reconstructs the sleeping body's sensory deprivation — dimmed sight, distorted hearing, dream-logic association — transforming somatic experience into polyphonic language.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish
Freud, Sigmund. The Interpretation of Dreams. https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/4349
Troy, Mark L. Mummeries of Resurrection. http://www.rosenlake.net

annotations.annotation_text: Fall/resurrection motif "broken" on page 442 ("Jaun's Sermon"): Tim Finnegan tumbling from his ladder, Humpty Dumpty shattering from the wall, Adam falling in Eden — all converge within Jaun (Shaun) preaching to the twenty-nine girls, the Ondt and the Gracehoper fable, departure and farewell. The comic-cosmic Fall during the Age of Men phase demands its counterpart: resurrection through the whiskey-splash of the water of life (uisce beatha).
sources: The Ballad of Tim Finnegan's Wake. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finnegan%27s_Wake
Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe
Opie, Iona and Peter. The Oxford Dictionary of Nursery Rhymes. https://archive.org/details/oxforddictionary0000unse_m4u1
